operator_instruction.text: Design and queue the MUSDB18-HQ stem-removal job left unscheduled in 126 (contract + p2 pending).

launch_authorization.scope: score ~40k pre-built 10 s clips (metric_win_tie_126c_stimuli.py, CPU + htdemucs, already on NVMe): up to 4 windows per MUSDB18-HQ track (150 tracks, all four stems active) x 65 cases (mix ref; tie: stem sum, htdemucs re-sum, single-stem +-1 dB, 126a tie signal variants; soft: +-3/+-6 dB rebalance, vocal phase-vocoder round trip; lose: drums lag 20-250 ms, vocals lag 50-250 ms, vocals detune 25-100 cents, bass +1 semitone, vocals/drums swapped from another song, 126a lose signal variants; descriptive: true stem removal, solo stem, htdemucs stem removal), all at -30 LUFS; AES + MEva + CLAP(batch 1, caption "music") + VGGish frames per clip; MIR on a CPU subprocess. No generation, no training.

question: In a real multitrack mix, do the metrics tie mix-balance and stem-sum changes, rank misaligned / detuned / swapped stems below the original, and is the score drop for removing drums or vocals a content effect (true stem removal) or a separation-artifact effect (htdemucs removal)?

fixed_protocol.stimuli: /home/kojiek/eval_output_nvme/metric_win_tie_126c_20261019/stimuli/items.json (36,366 rows, 551 windows, 145 tracks; built 2026-10-19 by scripts/eval/metric_win_tie_126c_stimuli.py --stage prep/demucs/build)
fixed_protocol.judgment: delta = score(case) - score(mix, same window); tie if |delta| <= m, m = 0.10 S; S = 126a S for neural metrics, SD of 126c mix clips for MIR; pass = 80 % of pairs; ladders report tolerance (tie) / detection (lose) steps
fixed_protocol.cross: separation artifact: dmx_no_<stem> vs no_<stem> per window; pitch error net of processing: vocals_detune vs vocal_pv0; by_group train/test (htdemucs trained on MUSDB train)
fixed_protocol.fad: VGGish frames per clip (float16); FAD per case vs the mix clips of the same windows
fixed_protocol.reading: human anchor is descriptive only: AES public MUSDB test mixture/stem ratings (full tracks, not our windows) vs mean d(only_<stem>); PC and MIR have no human validation here

resume.note: unit-level restart: a unit with matching keys, done.json and vggish_frames is skipped; a partial one is redone whole; mir.json skipped if present

completion_evidence.method: guest writes terminal with sha256 of the registered summary after --validate-only passes
